title: Brainrot Fusion
premise: A chaotic meme-themed physics merge game where the player drops oddball orb characters into a pit and fuses matching ones into larger, stranger forms before the stack reaches the warning line.
interaction_model: Single-screen mouse-and-touch arcade play: move horizontally to aim the drop lane, then tap or click to release the current orb into a shared physics container.
objective: Score as high as possible by creating repeated same-tier merges, building toward the highest evolution tier, and preventing the pile from settling into the top danger zone.
progression: Endless score attack progression with a seven-tier merge ladder; only small early-tier pieces spawn directly, while larger forms are earned through successful merges and chain building.
theme: Internet-brainrot meme chaos with neon arcade styling, emoji-faced fusion orbs, slang particles, and exaggerated reaction feedback.
mood: Goofy, loud, frantic, playful, and slightly absurd.
likely_audience: players who enjoy short arcade score-chasing sessions
confidence_notes: High confidence in the core mechanics because all gameplay logic is visible in a single HTML file.
High confidence that this is a Suika-like physics merge stacker with arcade score attack structure.
Moderate confidence in thematic interpretation; the 'brainrot' framing appears mostly cosmetic and comedic rather than narrative.
recreation_prompt: Create a single-screen browser arcade game called "Brainrot Fusion" that plays like a chaotic meme-themed Suika-style merge puzzler. The player controls a drop lane at the top of the screen by moving the mouse or dragging a finger horizontally, then taps or clicks to release the current orb into a full-screen physics pit. Each orb is a glossy circular character with an emoji or icon face, and matching tiers merge on contact into the next bigger form. Use a seven-step evolution ladder that starts with small goofy pieces like a skull, clown, and coin, then escalates into larger absurd meme-like forms such as a moai, alien, brain, and a final cosmic orb. Only the first few small tiers should spawn naturally, so bigger pieces must be earned through merges. Make the goal pure score attack survival: players try to set up clean merges, create combo momentum, and keep the pile from settling above a warning line near the top. If any settled stack remains inside that top danger zone for too long, trigger game over. Present everything with neon purple-cyan arcade visuals, a full-screen canvas, floating slang words in the background, a large flashy title screen, a compact HUD showing score and the next piece, and strong feedback juice including background music, drop/bump/merge/fail sound effects, and funny animated reaction media for merges and failure. Keep the controls simple, the pacing immediate, the tone silly and over-the-top, and the session structure endless with restart-on-loss rather than levels or story.
